title: ISO/IEC 42005:2025 — Terms and Definitions — Scope
text:
ISO/IEC 42005:2025 Terms and Definitions (Clause 3)

For the purposes of this document, the terms and definitions given in ISO/IEC 22989, ISO/IEC 23053 and the following apply.

This standard provides guidance for organizations performing AI system impact assessments (AISIA) for individuals and societies that can be affected by an AI system and its foreseeable applications.

Terms 3.1–3.9 are defined below. Section 4 provides abbreviated terms used throughout the standard.

title: AI system impact assessment
text:
3.1 AI system impact assessment

Definition: Formal, documented process by which the impacts to individuals, groups of individuals and societies are considered by an organization developing, providing, or using products or services utilizing artificial intelligence.

Context: This standard (ISO/IEC 42005:2025) provides detailed guidance on how to implement the AISIA process required by ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 6.1.4 and 8.4.

title: intended use
text:
3.2 intended use

Definition: Use for which an AI system is designed.

title: unintended use
text:
3.3 unintended use

Definition: Use for which an AI system is not designed.

title: intended users
text:
3.4 intended users

Definition: Groups of people or information systems for which an AI system is designed.

[SOURCE: ISO 20282-1:2006, 3.12, modified — "people" has been replaced with "people or information systems" and "a product" has been replaced with "an AI system".]

title: interested party
text:
3.5 interested party (stakeholder)

Definition: Person or organization that can affect, be affected by, or perceive itself to be affected by a decision or activity.

[SOURCE: ISO/IEC 42001:2023, 3.2]

title: reasonably foreseeable misuse
text:
3.6 reasonably foreseeable misuse

Definition: Use of an AI system in a way not intended by the AI system developer or provider, but which can result from readily predictable behaviour of intended users.

Note 1 to entry: Readily predictable human behaviour includes the behaviour of all types of users, e.g. the elderly, children and persons with disabilities. For more information, see ISO 10377.

Note 2 to entry: In the context of consumer safety, the term "reasonably foreseeable use" is increasingly used as a synonym for "intended use", and "unintended use" as a synonym for "reasonably foreseeable misuse."

Note 3 to entry: The specific definitions can vary somewhat, depending on the specific application area of the standard or regulation.

[SOURCE: ISO/IEC Guide 51:2014, 3.7, modified — "a product or system" has been replaced with "an AI system", and "supplier" has been replaced with "AI system developer or provider".]

title: restricted use
text:
3.7 restricted use

Definition: Use of an AI system that is constrained by laws, organizational policies or contractual agreements.

title: sensitive use
text:
3.8 sensitive use

Definition: Use of an AI system that can have a significant adverse impact on individuals, group of individuals or societies.

title: top management
text:
3.9 top management

Definition: Person or group of people who directs and controls an organization at the highest level.

Note 1 to entry: Top management has the power to delegate authority and provide resources within the organization.

Note 2 to entry: If the scope of the management system covers only part of an organization, then top management refers to those who direct and control that part of the organization.

[SOURCE: ISO/IEC 42001:2023, 3.3]
